gumroad_listing.title: Remote Work Policy Database 2026 — 1,000+ Companies Verified (CSV)
gumroad_listing.description:
Remote work policies for 1,000+ major US employers — verified from company career pages, press releases, and news coverage. The transparency job seekers desperately need but can't find. $39 one-time purchase.

**What you get:**
- Company name and industry
- HQ location (city, state)
- Policy type: Fully Remote, Hybrid, or Office-Required
- Days-in-office requirement (for hybrid companies: 2-day, 3-day, 4-day, flexible)
- Location flexibility: Work from anywhere, same metro area, or same state
- Policy last updated date
- Verification source URL (career page, press release, news article)
- Headcount tier: Startup (50-500), Mid-market (500-5K), or Enterprise (5K+)
- Policy change history (e.g., "Shifted from full-remote to 3-day hybrid in Sept 2023")
- Executive quote (where available) from CEO memos and announcements

**Coverage:**
- Fortune 500 companies: 400+ entries
- Major tech companies (FAANG, unicorns, public SaaS): 300+ entries
- High-growth startups (Series B-D): 200+ entries
- Financial services, consulting, healthcare, retail: 100+ entries
- Total: 1,000+ companies, 850+ with verified current policies (as of May 2026)

**Why job seekers buy this:**
- 91% of job seekers ask about remote work during interviews
- 84% are willing to reject offers without flexible arrangements
- But you're stuck Googling company names + "remote work policy" and getting outdated Reddit threads
- Career pages say "flexible work options" without specifying 2-day vs. 4-day hybrid
- Glassdoor reviews conflict ("fully remote" vs. "just announced RTO")
- Recruiter calls waste your time if policy is a dealbreaker

Stop researching policies one company at a time. Filter 1,000 companies in 10 seconds.

**Example filters:**
- "Show me all fully remote tech companies with 500-5,000 employees" → 47 results
- "Show me hybrid companies requiring 2 days or less in SF Bay Area" → 83 results
- "Show me companies that shifted FROM full-remote TO hybrid since 2023" → 134 results (culture warning flags)

**Who uses this:**
- Job seekers building target company lists for applications
- Recruiters benchmarking policies during initial screen calls
- Career coaches advising clients on offer negotiations
- Talent acquisition teams analyzing competitor policies
- Remote work advocates tracking industry trends

**Why $39 beats free sources:**
- Reddit/Blind: Unverified, conflicting, often outdated
- Glassdoor: Reviews are 6-18 months old, policies change fast
- Company career pages: Generic "flexible work" language, no specifics
- LinkedIn/Indeed job posts: Inconsistent, role-specific, not company-wide
- Scoop Flex Index: Tracks 9,000 companies but NOT accessible to individual job seekers (enterprise B2B tool)
- Manual research: 2-3 hours per company × 25 applications = 50-75 hours of your time

This database is verified, structured, filterable, and yours forever. No subscription. No monthly fees.

**Data source:** Public company announcements — career pages, press releases, news articles, executive memos. No employee surveys, no leaked internal docs, no scraping behind auth. Updated as of May 2026.

**Important:** Policies can change. Verification date included for every entry. Use source URLs to confirm current status before major career decisions. Not career advice — do your own due diligence.
